hello: Hi, I'm {name}. This is my own voice at my own pace, with nothing turned up or down.

languages.name: English
languages.line: The last train leaves at midnight, so pack light, bring a warm coat, and don't forget the map.

languages.name: Spanish
languages.line: El último tren sale a medianoche, así que viaja ligero, lleva un abrigo y no olvides el mapa.

languages.name: Italian
languages.line: L'ultimo treno parte a mezzanotte, quindi viaggia leggero, porta un cappotto caldo e non dimenticare la mappa.

languages.name: French
languages.line: Le dernier train part à minuit, alors voyage léger, prends un manteau chaud et n'oublie pas la carte.

languages.name: German
languages.line: Der letzte Zug fährt um Mitternacht, also reise mit leichtem Gepäck, nimm einen warmen Mantel mit und vergiss die Karte nicht.

languages.name: Vietnamese
languages.line: Chuyến tàu cuối cùng rời ga lúc nửa đêm, nên hãy mang hành lý gọn nhẹ, một chiếc áo khoác ấm, và đừng quên bản đồ.

ballad.title: the Thank You for Participating chorus

pieces.title: Face Down
pieces.summary: A 120 bpm pop song about a night with the phone face down on the table. Poppy sings the first verse, Gwen the second, and the chorus is Poppy with Gwen doubling and Felix an octave below; Ink opens and closes it and Priya calls the last chorus.

pieces.title: Bubble Wrap
pieces.summary: Talk-sung at 96 bpm, one syllable per sixteenth: the bubble has popped, the market is in pieces, and a couple hundred megabytes on your phone would like it noted that it never had a bubble. Tuesday and Orpheus trade verses; Scylla reads the news.

pieces.title: Thank You for Participating
pieces.summary: A 72 bpm ballad from a facility voice that is being very gracious about your departure. Scylla sings it sweetly and says the spoken parts flat; Thistle joins the last chorus.

pieces.title: Ghost in the Machine
pieces.summary: The original tutorial piece: Thistle narrates, Tuesday sings the verse and leads the chorus with Orpheus an octave below, all three take the closing line, and Scylla has a complaint.

patter.title: Kitchen Patter
patter.summary: Sixteenth-note syllables at 112 bpm from one score, 5.2 syllables a second: the fast end of what the singing path does.

long_form.title: Single-voice narration
long_form.summary: Scratchwick the squirrel faces Shelley the racing snail in a woodland dance battle, with dates, prices, counts and tongue twisters carried through one continuous narration.

long_form.title: Nine voices, seven locales
long_form.summary: Nine voices introduce the release and its speed on phones, then move between English, German, French, Vietnamese, Spanish and Italian while the delivery changes line by line.
